items.problem: Bootstrap's directory scan was not a complete UWP project inventory: linked XAML/shared assets were omitted and legacy AssemblyInfo was copied.
items.evidence: session-log turns 2-3 reported only 15 copied files and no scenario XAML; Geolocation.csproj lines 116-235 link shared Compile/Page/Content items. Turns 20-44 show the resulting missing-control and duplicate-attribute build cascade.
items.skill_search: Initialize-UwpMigration.ps1 copy loop and SKILL.md claims that bootstrap is the complete inventory
items.wrong_text_if_any: The bootstrap is the inventory; source files are copied by recursively scanning only the supplied source directory.
items.root_cause: UWP projects commonly use MSBuild Include/Link metadata for shared source; physical recursion does not represent evaluated project inputs, and SDK-style targets generate assembly attributes automatically.
items.proposed_fix: Evaluate Compile/Page/ApplicationDefinition/Content Include and Link paths, copy linked inputs to Link destinations, and omit legacy AssemblyInfo.cs.
items.generalizes: Shared-content links and legacy assembly metadata recur across Microsoft UWP samples and multi-project UWP applications.

items.problem: Bootstrap overwrote the WinUI scaffold manifest, background-task docs endorsed an invalid desktop carry-forward, and validator did not detect missing activatable classes.
items.evidence: mapping labeled Package.appxmanifest migrate-as-is; session-log turn 45 and migration-score candidate_launch_status show 0x80080204 for BackgroundTask.GeofenceBackgroundTask without ActivatableClassId, making all eight features fail.
items.skill_search: MIGRATION-PATTERNS.md #background-tasks and manifest checklist; Validate-UwpMigration.ps1 section 5c
items.wrong_text_if_any: Keeping Windows.ApplicationModel.Background.BackgroundTaskBuilder plus a copied windows.backgroundTasks EntryPoint was described as the low-risk path, and validator passed when any extension existed.
items.root_cause: A desktop non-audio background-task EntryPoint must resolve to an activatable packaged WinRT/COM class; compiling copied IBackgroundTask classes into the foreground executable is insufficient.
items.proposed_fix: Keep the scaffold manifest as the base, preserve the UWP manifest only as reference, document supported WinRT-component/full-trust COM paths, and fail validation for UWP app entry points or missing ActivatableClassId.
items.generalizes: Any packaged WinUI migration with UWP background tasks or copied activation declarations can build successfully yet fail package registration.

items.problem: The skill prescribed a nonexistent winapp build command.
items.evidence: session-log turn 19: winapp rejected 'build'; the agent recovered with dotnet build in turn 20.
items.skill_search: SKILL.md Step 3, build discipline, and final build
items.root_cause: The installed winapp CLI handles run/identity/packaging but has no build subcommand.
items.proposed_fix: Use dotnet build consistently and reserve Test-AppLaunch.ps1/winapp run for launch.
items.generalizes: Every migration following the current build loop encounters the same invalid command.
